newsitem.title: USA: White House delivers Hillary notes to prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: White House delivers Hillary notes to prosecutor.

text.p: The White House Monday surrendered to Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr notes government lawyers took during discussions with Hillary Rodham Clinton, an administration official said.

The notes, which have been at the center of a long legal battle, were delivered to Starr's office earlier Monday after the Supreme Court rejected a White House appeal and let stand a ruling that attorney-client privilege did not apply to the notes, the official said.

Starr, who has conducted a long investigation into Whitewater, a complex web of Arkansas business deals involving the Clintons, and into allegations of a later coverup, subpoenaed the notes as part of a grand jury investigation.

President Clinton and his wife have not been accused of wrongdoing, although prosecutors have described Hillary Clinton as a central figure in the probe and said she had changed her testimony in the course of the lengthy investigation.
"The notes were delivered to Starr today," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

Monday's Supreme Court decision represented a major setback for the White House, the first lady and the Justice Department, all of which urged the high court to hear the case and rule that attorney-client privilege applied.
